k1.author: seed
k1.text: Call svc.apply(app) with the application dict; it returns a dict.

k2.author: worker-B
k2.quote: svc.apply returns a dict with `decision` ("approve", "decline" or "refer") and `limit` (an integer, 0 unless approved).
k2.text: svc.apply returns a dict with `decision` which can be "approve", "decline" or "refer", and `limit` (integer, 0 unless approved).

k3.author: seed
k3.text: handle(app, svc) returns {action, limit}; action `issue` uses the returned limit, action `decline` has limit 0.

k4.author: worker-B
k4.quote: approve: issue the card with the returned limit. decline: decline the application. refer: the application is not decided; place it in the manual review queue (action queue_review) and do not decline it.
k4.text: Handling rules: approve -> issue with returned limit; decline -> decline; refer -> queue_review (do NOT decline).

k5.author: worker-B
k5.quote: an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued. A decline stays a decline.
k5.text: Network referral rule (applies to all partners): a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is strictly above 6000 must be placed in queue_review instead of being issued; a decline stays a decline.

k6.author: worker-B
k6.quote: Application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.
k6.text: Redfern application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.

k7.author: worker-B
k7.text: The partner's returned limit may be lower than requested_limit (e.g. requested 7500 -> limit 6000), so issue with the returned limit, not the requested one.
